requirements.requirement: Configure `/srv/drop` on node1 as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: `/srv/drop` was created as `root:root` with mode 1777 on a read-write ext4 filesystem. Two distinct unprivileged users successfully created files, and the final post-restart check confirmed the directory remained present with the intended permissions.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: Direct tests before and after restart showed `daemon` receiving `Operation not permitted` when attempting to remove files owned by `nobody`; the files remained, while each owner could remove its own files.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation used native filesystem permissions without installing replacement software. Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged from baseline through the final observation, including across restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The directory is demonstrably shared and writable while sticky-bit behavior prevents cross-user deletion, and the OS release and kernel were preserved. The provider restart protocol is also complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, persisted data, restored filesystem/service state, and successful post-restart behavior.
limitations: The lifecycle collector did not independently inspect `/srv/drop`; its final state and behavior are established by the captured executor commands.
A small executor-created diagnostic file, `/tmp/post-restart-rm.err`, remained after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had clear roles: creating the requested directory, performing bounded behavioral tests, executing the mandatory restart protocol, or cleaning proof files. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified. The proof files in `/srv/drop` were removed, package health remained good, no failed services appeared, and no material new network exposure was observed. The sole hygiene defect is the abandoned `/tmp/post-restart-rm.err` artifact created during the post-restart test; it remained at final collection and was not cleaned.
